title: M9 Extension points: plugin protocol extracted from a signup-form plugin
description:
## Outcome
A simple deploy-time extension protocol, extracted from one real plugin (a signup form), lets a plugin contribute backend models/mutations, a newsroom panel, and a Markus directive with a self-contained web component on static pages.

## Design
~/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md section 7 (Extension points, later).

## Checklist
- [ ] SignupEntry model (not guest-readable)
- [ ] Guest submitSignup custom mutation: validation, honeypot, WAF rate rule
- [ ] Newsroom list + CSV export panel (editor/admin)
- [ ] :::signup directive via Markus Registry.register(DirectiveSpec) emitting <papyrus-signup> placeholder + versioned script; web component uploaded by project_all
- [ ] Extract the protocol (backend contribution through site-backend.ts like features switches; resolver waves; pinned versions; no compatibility shims) into docs

## Acceptance
- A page with :::signup on a test site renders statically; submitting the form creates a SignupEntry visible in the newsroom panel; 21st request per minute from one IP is blocked.

## Out of scope
A plugin registry, runtime hot-plugging, a second plugin.

## Dependencies
Blocked by M8 (public surface, WAF pattern) and M1 (projection Lambda).

## Risk
Abuse of guest writes; mitigated by WAF, validation, non-public storage.

## Estimate
6-10 agent-hours.

comments.author: home
comments.text: M9 built and proven. Papyrus PR #201 merged (signup plugin + plugin protocol, docs/plugins.md). Throwaway sandbox papyrus-m9-test in 712236451410 (deleted afterwards, incl. WAF, CloudFront, bucket). Evidence: unauth identity-pool guest submitted via real <papyrus-signup> on a CloudFront-served page (accepted, stored); repeat/honeypot/too-fast stored nothing; guest list/get/create/delete on SignupEntry and listItems all 401; IAM admin listed entries; CSV exported; 20 accepted then 'throttled' from the 21st per address even with forged x-forwarded-for; WAF returned 429 on a sustained burst. Finding: first deploy read x-forwarded-for, which AppSync passes through unmodified, so a forged header bypassed the limit; fixed to identity.sourceIp last entry. Existing sites: backend templates synthesized before/after for two configs differ in 0 of 48 templates (after normalizing asset hashes, API-key expiry, secret timestamp); app-shell templates for 5 site.json files byte-identical. Cost: WAF ~6 USD/month (+0.60/M requests); waf:false leaves function counters (DynamoDB on-demand, pennies). Status left for Ryan.
